overview: Gartner is the world's leading IT and business research and advisory firm, delivering actionable insights, data, and expert guidance to executives across nearly every industry through subscription-based research, in-person and virtual conferences, and bespoke consulting engagements. Founded in 1979 and headquartered in Stamford, Connecticut, the company operates through three reportable segments — Insights (formerly Research), Conferences, and Consulting — serving roughly 15,000+ client enterprises across the Americas, EMEA, and Asia-Pacific. FY2025 revenue was approximately $6.5 billion, though the stock has been under significant pressure since February 2026 after contract-value growth decelerated sharply and management disclosed a consulting-revenue shortfall, triggering securities litigation.

business_model.summary: Gartner's core economic engine is the Insights (research) segment, which sells annual subscription access to syndicated research, benchmarking data, and one-on-one analyst inquiry — a high-margin, highly recurring model that historically drove 80%+ of revenue and the bulk of profitability. Conferences (Symposium/Xpo and role-based events) monetize the same research content and analyst relationships through ticketed, in-person/hybrid events with an exhibitor-sponsorship component. Consulting is project- and staff-augmentation-based, leveraging Gartner's research IP for bespoke advisory work (IT cost optimization, digital transformation, sourcing) and is the most cyclical, lowest-margin, and currently most challenged segment — full-year 2025 consulting revenue of ~$552M missed the company's own $575M guidance and declined versus 2024. In February 2026 Gartner completed the ~$110M sale of its Digital Markets business (Capterra, Software Advice, GetApp) to G2, simplifying the portfolio around the three core segments. The Insights business is priced and renewed via 'Contract Value' (CV), Gartner's key forward-looking KPI (12-month forward-looking value of subscription contracts), which is disclosed quarterly and has become the single most-watched (and most controversial) metric in the story.

revenue_streams.name: Insights (Research subscriptions)
revenue_streams.trend: decelerating growth, still the core profit engine

business_model.customer_type: B2B enterprise — CIOs, CTOs, CFOs, supply chain, HR, marketing and other functional executives across corporate, government, and mid-market organizations; entry-level research subscriptions typically run $25,000-$60,000+ per year per contract
business_model.geographic_mix: United States/Americas the largest market (majority of revenue), with EMEA and Asia-Pacific as smaller but growing international segments; federal/government (GTS Federal) is a distinct, currently weaker sub-segment cited in recent results (DOGE-related federal spending disruption)

main_competitors: in-house analytics/AI tools (including generative AI assistants)
competitive_position.market_position: Gartner is the dominant #1 player in IT research and advisory, roughly an order of magnitude larger by revenue than its nearest direct research-model peer, Forrester (~$430M revenue vs. Gartner's ~$6.5B). It competes with strategy consultancies (McKinsey, BCG, Bain, Accenture) when engagements shift from ongoing research subscriptions to large-scale transformation projects, and increasingly faces disintermediation risk from generative AI tools that can synthesize publicly available market information.

moat_factors.description: Roughly 21,000 employees and thousands of analysts covering virtually every technology and business function create a depth and breadth of proprietary research, peer benchmarking data, and vendor evaluation (Magic Quadrant) content that smaller competitors cannot easily replicate.

Gartner research and analyst inquiry access is embedded in enterprise IT and procurement decision workflows (vendor selection, budget benchmarking, board reporting), creating real switching costs and multi-year renewal patterns, historically evidenced by Insights net revenue retention in the mid-90s% to low-100s%.

The 'Gartner Magic Quadrant' and similar frameworks are industry-standard shorthand referenced in enterprise RFPs and vendor marketing; Gartner's perceived independence (it does not sell to the vendors it rates, unlike some consultancies) reinforces credibility.

A large, tenured enterprise sales organization cross-sells Insights, Conferences, and Consulting into the same accounts, historically supporting high win-rates on renewals and expansions — though this same sales-execution engine has been the source of the 2025-2026 CV growth shortfall.
Aggregated, anonymized client data (IT spend benchmarks, peer surveys) becomes more valuable as the client base grows, a modest data-network effect that smaller competitors lack at scale.

weaknesses: Contract Value growth has collapsed from a historical medium-term target of 12-16% to roughly 1% at the FY2025 trough (ex-Fed CV improved only modestly to ~3.3% by Q2 2026), calling into question whether the growth algorithm investors underwrote is intact
Consulting segment revenue is shrinking (-8.8% YoY in Q2 2026) and has repeatedly missed management's own guidance, exposing a structurally weaker, project-based part of the business
Federal/government contract value has been disrupted by DOGE-related federal spending cuts, a discrete and largely uncontrollable headwind

Increasing generative-AI disintermediation risk: enterprise executives can now use ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot, and other LLMs to synthesize public market information that previously required a Gartner subscription, potentially compressing the perceived value of lower-tier research access
Active securities class-action litigation and a fresh (September 2026) shareholder/fiduciary-duty investigation create legal overhang, distraction, and potential monetary/reputational costs
Lengthening enterprise buying cycles and deferred IT decision-making have structurally slowed new/expansion bookings, a trend management has acknowledged took longer to reverse than originally guided

growth_drivers: Contract Value reacceleration: ex-Fed CV growth improved roughly 70bps sequentially in Q2 2026 to 3.3%, which management is framing as the first evidence of stabilization after the 2025 trough; full recovery toward the historical 12-16% algorithm (or even high-single-digit growth) would be the single biggest re-rating catalyst

AI-related research demand: management has cited 'strong demand for AI-related insights' as clients seek independent guidance on evaluating, pricing, and managing risk from AI vendors (OpenAI, Anthropic, Microsoft Copilot, Google) — a potential new secular growth vector that plays to Gartner's core competency of vendor-neutral research

Conferences segment momentum: +15% YoY revenue growth in Q2 2026, showing that in-person/flagship events (Symposium/Xpo, IT, Data & Analytics, Security & Risk summits) remain in high demand and carry attractive incremental margins

Capital allocation/buybacks: Gartner repurchased $547M of stock in Q2 2026 alone and increased its buyback authorization by $500M in July 2026, aggressively retiring shares (diluted share count down from ~90M in 2020 to ~67M by Q2 2026) at what management evidently views as a depressed valuation post the February 2026 selloff

Portfolio simplification: the February 2026 sale of the lower-margin, non-core Digital Markets business (Capterra/Software Advice/GetApp) for ~$110M sharpens focus on the core three-segment model and removes a distraction
International and mid-market expansion of Insights subscriptions outside the historically penetrated large-enterprise US base

business.risk: Contract Value growth deceleration/uncertain recovery trajectory
business.description: CV growth fell from a historically guided 12-16% medium-term algorithm to roughly 1% at the FY2025 trough; while Q2 2026 showed sequential improvement to ~3.3% ex-Fed, it remains far below the algorithm management spent years promoting, and the durability of the nascent recovery is unproven.

Consulting revenue fell 8.8% YoY in Q2 2026 and FY2025 consulting revenue missed the company's own guidance for a second consecutive year, suggesting either demand softness, execution issues, or both in the project-based advisory business.

LLM-based tools increasingly allow enterprise buyers to self-serve market synthesis that previously required a paid Gartner subscription, a long-term risk to the perceived value of lower-tier research products even as Gartner also monetizes AI-advisory demand.
DOGE-related federal budget cuts and contract disruptions materially weakened the GTS Federal contract-value book through 2025, a discrete headwind outside Gartner's control.

business.risk: Sales execution and lengthening buying cycles
business.description: Management has repeatedly cited a tougher selling environment with clients deferring decisions and elongated purchase cycles, indicating either macro softness in enterprise IT budgets or an internal sales-execution gap (or both) that has not yet been fully resolved.

financial.risk: Goodwill impairment risk in non-core units
financial.description: Gartner recorded a $150.0M goodwill impairment in the Digital Markets reporting unit in Q3 2025 (ahead of the unit's February 2026 sale), evidence that non-core assets can carry meaningful write-down risk.

Net debt/EBITDA around 1.3x is moderate, but the pace of buybacks ($547M in Q2 2026 alone, plus a $500M authorization increase) is aggressive relative to free cash flow generation and could constrain balance-sheet flexibility if CV growth disappoints again.
Meaningful non-US revenue exposes reported results to a stronger dollar; management has flagged FX as a guidance headwind even while raising underlying targets.

regulatory.description: Multiple law firms have filed securities fraud class actions alleging Gartner and its officers made misleading statements about CV growth (projecting 12-16% growth while actual growth fell to ~1%) and inflated consulting revenue outlook; a lead plaintiff deadline occurred in mid-2026 and the case(s) remain unresolved, creating potential monetary liability and reputational risk.

As of September 2026, firms including Bernstein Liebhard and Bronstein, Gewirtz & Grossman announced active investigations into potential breaches of fiduciary duty by Gartner directors/officers tied to the same disclosure issues underlying the securities litigation.

regulatory.risk: Data privacy and government contracting compliance
regulatory.description: Standard enterprise-research industry exposure to data-handling and, for the federal book, government contracting compliance requirements.

macro.description: Gartner's core Insights product is a discretionary line item within enterprise IT/G&A budgets; the 2025 CV slowdown coincided with clients deferring and elongating purchase decisions amid macro uncertainty, illustrating direct sensitivity to corporate spending sentiment even though the subscription model provides some buffer via multi-year contracts.
US federal government spending policy (DOGE-related cuts) had an outsized, largely non-diversifiable impact on the Federal contract-value book in 2025.

As a high-margin, subscription-like business trading on a growth/quality multiple, IT's valuation is moderately sensitive to the rate environment, though its current depressed multiple (forward P/E near 12x per the January 2026-vintage screen) limits further multiple-compression risk relative to history.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: The IT/business research and advisory industry is mature but still growing at a mid-single-digit rate globally, with an emerging tailwind from enterprise demand for independent guidance navigating AI vendor selection, pricing, and risk. Gartner itself is one of the most visible voices publishing on enterprise AI adoption risk (e.g., research on AI vendor risk management, ROI skepticism around AI-driven layoffs), positioning the category as both a source of disruption risk and incremental demand.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate. The subscription research model (Insights) is relatively resilient with high renewal rates, but Consulting is meaningfully cyclical and tied to discretionary enterprise transformation spending, and even Insights new/expansion bookings slow visibly when clients tighten IT budgets or elongate decision cycles, as seen through 2025.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low-to-moderate direct sensitivity; indirect sensitivity via enterprise capex/opex budget cycles and valuation multiple compression for growth-oriented names.
key_input_costs: Analyst and sales-force compensation (largest cost line)
Travel and event production costs for Conferences

recent_developments.event: Multiple law firms (Bernstein Liebhard, Bronstein Gewirtz & Grossman) announced fresh shareholder/fiduciary-duty investigations into Gartner directors and officers tied to the 2025-2026 contract-value and consulting-revenue disclosure controversy; RBC nonetheless raised its price target to $198 (from $164) while maintaining a Hold/Sector Perform rating, and the stock rose alongside renewed market focus on Gartner's AI-research positioning even amid the legal overhang.

Q2 2026 results reported: revenue $1.7B (+3% YoY reported), Adjusted EBITDA $466M (+6% YoY), Adjusted EPS +24% YoY, free cash flow $378M (+8.9% YoY), operating cash flow +3.8%. Segment detail: Insights revenue $1.29B (+2%), Conferences revenue $244M (+15%), Consulting revenue $142M (-8.8%). Contract Value ex-Fed grew 3.3%, with total CV YoY growth improving ~70bps versus Q1 2026 — the first sequential CV acceleration cited by management since the 2025 downturn began. Share repurchases totaled $547M in the quarter.
Board increased the share-repurchase authorization by $500M, signaling continued aggressive capital return alongside the CV-growth recovery narrative.

Securities fraud class actions continued to progress through 2026 (lead plaintiff deadlines, amended complaints) alleging Gartner and named officers made misleading statements projecting 12-16% medium-term Research Contract Value growth while actual CV growth fell from 7.8% (Q4 2024) to roughly 1% (by Q4 2025), and that FY2025 consulting revenue guidance (~$575M) was not achievable and ultimately missed (actual ~$552M).

Completed the sale of the Digital Markets business (Capterra, Software Advice, GetApp) to G2 for approximately $110.0M gross / ~$104.8M net of cash transferred, recording a $5.4M pre-tax gain in H1 2026; Digital Markets had previously been folded into the 'Other' segment after Q3 2025 restructuring.

Q4/FY2025 results reported alongside FY2026 guidance that badly missed elevated market expectations: FY2026 revenue guided to at least $6.455B (~2% FX-neutral growth) versus a market-implied ~$6.7B, and contract value ex-Fed growth of only ~4% (with total CV growth even lower). Stock fell over 20% intraday to a 52-week low as investors absorbed both the guidance miss and the first explicit disclosure that consulting revenue had structurally undershot prior guidance.

Q3 2025 results included a $150.0M goodwill impairment charge in the Digital Markets reporting unit (ahead of its eventual sale), driving reported operating income down to $86.3M from $245.8M a year earlier, even as management simultaneously raised full-year 2025 Adjusted EBITDA and margin guidance on an adjusted basis and reiterated an expectation for CV growth to accelerate into 2026.

Company underwent an internal operating-model transformation under Yvonne Genovese (leading Insights/Business & Technology Insights organization), including multiple rounds of role eliminations and restructuring across research analyst and support staff functions, framed by management as a deliberate cost/structure realignment to support renewed profitable growth rather than a reactive cut.

items.vs_prior: raised from original February 2026 guide of at least $6.455B on an FX-neutral constant basis (note: reported-dollar figure moved with FX; underlying operating metrics were raised)
items.notes: Raised despite a stronger US dollar headwind, reflecting Q2 outperformance and improving CV trends; investors should reconcile the FX-neutral vs. as-reported framing directly against the Q2 2026 press release given the divergence in reported figures across sources.

Raised alongside EPS and FCF guidance on the Q2 2026 call, cited by management as reflecting accelerating contract value growth, robust client engagement, and continued strong demand for AI-related insights.

items.vs_prior: raised from prior guidance given in Q1 2026
items.notes: Adjusted EPS grew 24% YoY in Q2 2026 alone, aided by the aggressive buyback program shrinking the diluted share count.
Q2 2026 FCF of $378M (+8.9% YoY) supports the raised full-year target.
Quarterly bridge toward the raised full-year EBITDA target.

items.target: continued sequential acceleration off the ~3.3% Q2 2026 print
items.vs_prior: improving vs. 2025 trough (~1% total CV growth), but still far below the previously communicated 12-16% medium-term algorithm
items.notes: This is the single most closely watched KPI in the stock; management has not reinstated a specific medium-term CV growth target following the 2025 guidance miss and subsequent litigation, instead focusing commentary on quarter-over-quarter sequential improvement.

guidance.management_commentary: On the Q2 2026 call, management characterized results as 'ahead of expectations' across revenue, EBITDA, adjusted EPS, and free cash flow, citing 'accelerating contract value growth, robust client engagement, and continued strong demand for AI-related insights' as the basis for raising full-year guidance even in the face of a stronger US dollar. Management continues to frame the 2025 cost actions and organizational restructuring (including changes to the Insights/research organization under new leadership) as deliberate steps to enable 'profitable growth in 2026 and beyond' rather than reactive austerity, while conspicuously avoiding reinstating the specific 12-16% medium-term CV growth algorithm that is now central to the pending securities litigation.

bull_case: Contract Value growth has bottomed and is inflecting: ex-Fed CV growth improved sequentially from Q1 to Q2 2026 (up ~70bps to 3.3%), and if this trajectory continues, a return toward even high-single-digit CV growth would likely drive a substantial re-rating given how depressed sentiment and the multiple became after the February 2026 collapse

Aggressive, well-funded capital return: $547M repurchased in a single quarter (Q2 2026) plus a fresh $500M authorization increase reflects management's confidence in intrinsic value and materially shrinks the share count (diluted shares down from ~90M in 2020 to ~67M by mid-2026), amplifying EPS growth even at modest revenue growth

AI-research demand is a genuine incremental tailwind, not just a risk: enterprises need independent, vendor-neutral guidance to navigate AI vendor selection, pricing, and risk exposure — exactly Gartner's historical value proposition — and management has explicitly cited this as a current demand driver

High-margin, highly recurring Insights subscription base with historically strong client retention provides a durable earnings floor even through the 2025-2026 growth trough, supporting continued strong free cash flow generation (guided at least $1.185B for FY2026) and dividend/buyback capacity

Valuation has reset meaningfully lower after the ~50%+ peak-to-trough stock decline, and even skeptical sell-side analysts (RBC, Hold-rated) have been raising price targets as results have come in ahead of the newly conservative post-February-2026 guidance bar
bear_case: The core growth algorithm investors underwrote for years (12-16% medium-term Contract Value growth) has been shown to be unreliable — actual CV growth collapsed to roughly 1% at the 2025 trough — and management has not reinstated any comparable medium-term target, leaving genuine uncertainty about what normalized growth looks like going forward

Active securities fraud class-action litigation alleges Gartner and named officers knowingly or recklessly made misleading statements about CV growth and consulting revenue outlook; regardless of ultimate merit, this creates legal cost, distraction, and reputational overhang, compounded by fresh September 2026 fiduciary-duty investigations

Consulting segment is in outright decline (-8.8% YoY in Q2 2026) with a second consecutive year of missing management's own guidance, raising questions about whether this is cyclical softness or a structural erosion of that business line

Generative AI increasingly allows enterprise buyers to self-serve market synthesis and vendor comparisons that previously required a paid Gartner subscription — a genuine long-term disintermediation risk to the core Insights product even as Gartner tries to monetize AI-advisory demand on the other side of the same trend

Federal spending disruption (DOGE-related cuts) demonstrated how exposed a meaningful part of the CV book is to policy risk outside management's control, and elongated enterprise buying cycles suggest the demand slowdown was broader than just the federal book
